coverage.checklistItem: Define what is launching and identify the exact release or commit.
coverage.note: The release, commit, content, and configuration scope must come from the project team.

coverage.checklistItem: Choose the launch window and assign the people responsible for deployment, testing, communications, and rollback.
coverage.note: Timing, ownership, and availability require project confirmation.

coverage.checklistItem: Define what would stop the launch or trigger a rollback.
coverage.note: Go/no-go and rollback rules depend on the release risk and business impact.

coverage.checklistItem: Record known issues, approve accepted risks, and tell stakeholders what is changing.
coverage.note: Known issues, risk acceptance, and communications require accountable human decisions.

coverage.checklistItem: Complete the reviews that apply to this launch: accessibility, security, performance, SEO, privacy, and release readiness.
coverage.note: The launch skill reuses supplied specialist evidence or confirmation and does not rerun those reviews automatically.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm there are no unresolved launch-blocking findings.
coverage.note: The decision owner must review current findings, accepted risks, and missing evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Test the release candidate in a production-like environment.
coverage.note: The public runner cannot establish whether the reviewed environment and release match production.

coverage.checklistItem: Review the homepage, navigation, important pages, forms, search, downloads, and error pages.
coverage.note: The runner reviews one homepage and bounded same-host link destinations. Important pages, forms, search, downloads, and error behavior remain project-specific tests.

coverage.checklistItem: Remove test content, placeholder text, draft material, and environment-specific values.
coverage.note: The screenshot and homepage summary help a reviewer spot obvious issues, but approved production content and configuration require human review.

coverage.checklistItem: Set up and verify that the site can send emails.
coverage.note: Email tests can notify people and require approved recipients, sender configuration, and failure evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm analytics, consent tools, important integrations, and production content are ready.
coverage.note: Correct production events, consent behavior, credentials, endpoints, and content approval require project evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Back up everything needed for recovery and confirm the backups can be restored.
coverage.note: Backup completeness and restoration require operational evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Write down the deployment, migration, smoke-test, and rollback steps.
coverage.note: Runbook steps must match the release, platform, owners, and available access.

coverage.checklistItem: Rehearse high-risk migrations or deployment steps before launch.
coverage.note: Rehearsal evidence depends on the actual deployment and migration procedure.

coverage.checklistItem: Prepare any DNS, certificate, redirect, or domain changes.
coverage.note: The runner observes the current public URL and bounded HTTP redirect. Planned DNS, certificates, redirects, and domain changes require the cutover plan.

coverage.checklistItem: Lower and later restore DNS TTLs when the cutover plan requires it.
coverage.note: TTL changes are conditional operational actions and are not made by the runner.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm production access, monitoring, support, and any necessary change freeze are ready.
coverage.note: Access, alerts, support availability, and change controls require operational confirmation.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm the approved release, configuration, content, and rollback point have not changed.
coverage.note: The decision owner must compare the approved and deployable release state.

coverage.checklistItem: Review open issues, current incidents, and unavailable dependencies.
coverage.note: Current issue, incident, and dependency status comes from project and operational systems.

coverage.checklistItem: Record the final go, delay, or no-go decision.
coverage.note: Codex makes an evidence-backed recommendation; the accountable decision owner records the final decision.

coverage.checklistItem: Deploy the approved release and any related database, content, DNS, or redirect changes.
coverage.note: The read-only preflight does not deploy or change external systems.

coverage.checklistItem: Remove maintenance mode, clear caches, and rebuild search indexes when the site is ready.
coverage.note: The runner observes the resulting homepage but does not change maintenance mode, caches, or search indexes.

coverage.checklistItem: Test critical pages, navigation, forms, email, search, authentication, and integrations.
coverage.note: The runner performs a homepage and link smoke review. State-changing and authenticated workflows require approved project tests.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm HTTPS, redirects, analytics, consent, canonicals, robots directives, and sitemaps.
coverage.note: The launch runner checks HTTPS, the bounded HTTP redirect, and homepage noindex signals. Prior technical SEO evidence and human checks cover the remaining signals.

coverage.checklistItem: Watch monitoring and support reports, and record problems or launch decisions.
coverage.note: Monitoring, support, and decision records require operational access and ownership.

coverage.checklistItem: Repeat critical tests after DNS, caches, search, and scheduled work have settled.
coverage.note: The same bounded preflight can be rerun later, but project-specific critical workflows remain manual or project-owned tests.

coverage.checklistItem: Check logs, monitoring, backups, forms, email, analytics, and scheduled jobs.
coverage.note: These checks require approved operational systems and, for forms or email, potentially state-changing tests.

coverage.checklistItem: Crawl the site for broken links, bad redirects, and indexing problems.
coverage.note: The runner checks a bounded same-host sample from one homepage. A representative crawl and prior technical SEO review cover the wider site.

coverage.checklistItem: Remove temporary settings and assign every remaining issue an owner.
coverage.note: Temporary settings and issue ownership depend on the cutover plan and project records.

coverage.checklistItem: **Recommended:** Update the runbook and tests with useful lessons from the launch.
coverage.note: The team decides which launch observations should become durable procedure or test improvements.

coverage.checklistItem: Stop the launch and use the approved rollback plan when a rollback trigger is met.
coverage.note: Only the authorized launch owner can stop the launch and invoke rollback.

coverage.checklistItem: Roll back code, database, redirects, and DNS changes as needed.
coverage.note: The read-only preflight does not alter code, data, redirects, or DNS.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm the recovered site works and reconcile data changed during the failed launch.
coverage.note: Recovery validation requires the restored environment, project-specific tests, and data reconciliation.

coverage.checklistItem: Tell stakeholders what happened, the current status, and the next step.
coverage.note: Stakeholder communication requires project ownership and approved messaging.
